Mosaic

Bring a class, a PDF, a video or a photo of your notebook. Mosaic transcribes it on your device, writes a note you can understand, then makes you explain it back, quiz yourself and watch it move, in English and French.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Students leave a class with a recording they never replay, slides, photos of the board and a PDF chapter. Rereading feels like studying but rarely sticks, and the tools are scattered: one app for notes, another for flashcards, another for transcription, most of them in English only and sending recordings to a server. French-speaking learners, in Cameroon especially, get the least.

02

What it does

Mosaic turns whatever a learner brings into a note they can study. A class recorded live or a video dropped in is transcribed on the device, with chapters whose times replay the exact moment. Claude writes the note as a document: the idea in plain words, an analogy, a roadmap, the explanation, a worked example, the words to explain and the traps. Then comes the Feynman path. Teach it back checks the learner's own explanation against the key ideas and says what is missing; a quiz, flashcards on spaced repetition and a mock exam follow. Visualize turns a passage into an animated, interactive explanation, such as a parabola with sliders or a device getting its address through DHCP. Around it sit a notebook with tags, tasks and a calendar, a PDF viewer with highlights, lessons with interactive models, a library, and Mentor, a study companion on every page that proposes actions the learner confirms. A guided demo loads a sample notebook and walks through every feature in 30 steps.

03

How it is built

Next.js 16 and React 19 in strict TypeScript, with Tailwind and next-intl for a complete English and French interface, hosted on Vercel; the editor is TipTap. Notes and original files stay in the browser. Whisper runs on the device in a worker, so recordings are never uploaded for transcription; only the transcript and a few still frames go to Claude to write the note. The Claude API also checks explanations and writes visual specifications that are validated for shape and meaning before they play, and sent back once for repair. Accounts and sync use Supabase Postgres with row-level security, documents use pdf.js, and flashcards are scheduled with FSRS. 536 unit and database tests and 210 end-to-end and accessibility tests (Playwright and axe) run on a production build, on a computer and a phone. Card payments are built on Stripe Checkout and stay off until the owner switches them on.
